findings.body: All calls recorded on the returned throwaway logger are lost; the injected TestLogger reports Calls==0 and Message=="", so log assertions silently pass/fail incorrectly and the new contextual logging path is effectively untestable.
findings.failure_mode: Test doubles lose recorded state, so the new logging behavior introduced by this patch cannot be verified.
findings.impact: All calls recorded on the returned throwaway logger are lost; the injected TestLogger reports Calls==0 and Message=="", so log assertions silently pass/fail incorrectly and the new contextual logging path is effectively untestable.
findings.root_cause: The newly added fake implementation of FromContext constructs a fresh TestLogger instead of returning the existing recorder.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the receiver (`return f`) so the fake keeps recording into the same Logs structs, matching the semantics of the real grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext which preserves the logger's state.
findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the receiver, making logged calls unobservable in tests
findings.trigger: A test injects a *plog.TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware (which now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)) and then asserts on the injected logger's InfoLogs.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch adds `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` at line 46-48. This returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so any calls logged on the returned logger are lost. LoggerMiddleware calls `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, meaning tests injecting TestLogger cannot observe logged calls.

<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

**What is this feature?**

- Renames the `InstrumentationMiddleware` to `MetricsMiddleware`
- Moves the contextual logger from the `Instrumentation/Metrics middleware` to the `LoggerMiddleware`

**Why do we need this feature?**

Better naming and consistency.

**Who is this feature for?**

Plugins platform.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

<!--

- Automatically closes linked issue when the Pull Request is merged.

Usage: "Fixes #<issue number>", or "Fixes (paste link of issue)"

-->

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.

raw_findings.body: All calls recorded on the returned throwaway logger are lost; the injected TestLogger reports Calls==0 and Message=="", so log assertions silently pass/fail incorrectly and the new contextual logging path is effectively untestable.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test doubles lose recorded state, so the new logging behavior introduced by this patch cannot be verified.
raw_findings.impact: All calls recorded on the returned throwaway logger are lost; the injected TestLogger reports Calls==0 and Message=="", so log assertions silently pass/fail incorrectly and the new contextual logging path is effectively untestable.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly added fake implementation of FromContext constructs a fresh TestLogger instead of returning the existing recorder.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return the receiver (`return f`) so the fake keeps recording into the same Logs structs, matching the semantics of the real grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext which preserves the logger's state.
raw_findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards the receiver, making logged calls unobservable in tests
raw_findings.trigger: A test injects a *plog.TestLogger into LoggerMiddleware (which now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", ...)) and then asserts on the injected logger's InfoLogs.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) — the fields LoggerMiddleware now depends on for its log line — would not be detected by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: New behavior ships without regression coverage.
raw_findings.impact: Regressions in the contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) — the fields LoggerMiddleware now depends on for its log line — would not be detected by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: Logic was moved into a new, untested middleware while its previous host file's test only covers prometheus metrics.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add contextual_logger_middleware_test.go asserting that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics propagate a context whose contextual attributes contain endpoint, pluginId and datasource/user fields.
raw_findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no unit test covering context enrichment
raw_findings.trigger: The patch adds a brand new middleware file and wires it into CreateMiddlewares, but adds no *_test.go for it; the moved instrumentContext logic is no longer covered by metrics_middleware_test.go either.

raw_findings.body: LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" line silently loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname, because those fields are no longer passed explicitly and only come from the contextual attributes injected upstream.
raw_findings.evidence:
// NewContextualLoggerMiddleware creates a new plugins.ClientMiddleware that adds
// a contextual logger to the request context.
raw_findings.failure_mode: An undocumented cross-middleware dependency can be broken by future edits without any compile or test signal.
raw_findings.impact: LoggerMiddleware's "Plugin Request Completed" line silently loses pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID and uname, because those fields are no longer passed explicitly and only come from the contextual attributes injected upstream.
raw_findings.root_cause: The ordering requirement documented on the old InstrumentationMiddleware was dropped when the responsibility was split into a separate middleware.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Document on NewContextualLoggerMiddleware that it must be registered above LoggerMiddleware (and near the top of the stack) so downstream middlewares can rely on the contextual attributes.
raw_findings.title: New middleware's doc comment omits the required ordering constraint that was deleted from the metrics middleware
raw_findings.trigger: The deleted comment on InstrumentationMiddleware ("this middleware should live at the top of the middleware stack") is not restated anywhere; a later change reorders CreateMiddlewares and puts NewContextualLoggerMiddleware after NewLoggerMiddleware.

raw_findings.body: The identifier (and its comment claiming it "adds a contextual logger") contradicts the PR's stated renaming goal and misdescribes the behavior, which is adding contextual log attributes, hindering future maintenance.
raw_findings.evidence: func instrumentContext(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, pCtx backend.PluginContext) context.Context {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Naming/documentation drift between the new file's purpose and its helper.
raw_findings.impact: The identifier (and its comment claiming it "adds a contextual logger") contradicts the PR's stated renaming goal and misdescribes the behavior, which is adding contextual log attributes, hindering future maintenance.
raw_findings.root_cause: Code was moved verbatim into the new file without renaming it to match the new middleware's responsibility.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename to something like withContextualLogAttributes and update the comment to say it adds plugin/request log attributes to the context.
raw_findings.title: Moved helper keeps the misleading name instrumentContext in the contextual logger middleware
raw_findings.trigger: Reading contextual_logger_middleware.go after the PR renames instrumentation concerns to metrics; the function no longer belongs to any "instrumentation" middleware and only attaches log attributes.

raw_findings.body: Identifier no longer matches the type it holds, leaving a leftover reference to the removed InstrumentationMiddleware naming this PR set out to eliminate.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incomplete rename leaves inconsistent naming in the changed function.
raw_findings.impact: Identifier no longer matches the type it holds, leaving a leftover reference to the removed InstrumentationMiddleware naming this PR set out to eliminate.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rename was applied to types and functions but not to local variables derived from the old name.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the local variable to `mw` (or `mmw`) consistent with MetricsMiddleware.
raw_findings.title: Stale abbreviation `imw` retained after renaming to MetricsMiddleware
raw_findings.trigger: Reading NewMetricsMiddleware after the rename; `imw` stands for "instrumentation middleware", a type that no longer exists.

raw_findings.body: Test output and `go test -run` selectors reference a middleware name that no longer exists, contradicting the rename goal of this PR and making the test harder to locate.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale test naming survives the rename, leaving inconsistent references to a deleted type.
raw_findings.impact: Test output and `go test -run` selectors reference a middleware name that no longer exists, contradicting the rename goal of this PR and making the test harder to locate.
raw_findings.root_cause: The rename covered the file name and the constructor call but not the test function identifier.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the test function to TestMetricsMiddleware in metrics_middleware_test.go as part of this rename.
raw_findings.title: Renamed test file still declares TestInstrumentationMiddleware
raw_findings.trigger: After this patch, instrumentation_middleware_test.go is renamed to metrics_middleware_test.go and its body updated to call newMetricsMiddleware, but the enclosing test function is still `func TestInstrumentationMiddleware(t *testing.T)` (the only remaining occurrence of "InstrumentationMiddleware" in the repo).

raw_findings.body: Those implementations no longer satisfy plog.Logger and fail to compile with "missing method FromContext", breaking downstream builds.
raw_findings.evidence:
// FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context.
	FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger
raw_findings.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage for out-of-tree implementations of the exported interface.
raw_findings.impact: Those implementations no longer satisfy plog.Logger and fail to compile with "missing method FromContext", breaking downstream builds.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new required method was added to an exported interface without an adapter or default implementation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Verify/patch all in-tree and downstream implementers of plog.Logger, or provide an embeddable default implementation so adding the method is non-breaking; note the breaking change in the PR description.
raw_findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported plugins log.Logger interface breaks external implementers
raw_findings.trigger: Any code outside this repository tree (e.g. Grafana Enterprise or other consumers of pkg/plugins/log) that implements plog.Logger and passes it to NewLoggerMiddleware or backendplugin logging is compiled against the new interface.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Stylistic concern about test function name `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` not being renamed. The test still works correctly, the function name doesn't affect test execution. This is a naming consistency preference, not a defect.

validated_findings.body: Those implementations no longer satisfy plog.Logger and fail to compile with "missing method FromContext", breaking downstream builds.
validated_findings.evidence:
// FromContext returns a new contextual Logger that has this logger's context plus the given context.
	FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger
validated_findings.failure_mode: Compile-time breakage for out-of-tree implementations of the exported interface.
validated_findings.impact: Those implementations no longer satisfy plog.Logger and fail to compile with "missing method FromContext", breaking downstream builds.
validated_findings.root_cause: A new required method was added to an exported interface without an adapter or default implementation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Verify/patch all in-tree and downstream implementers of plog.Logger, or provide an embeddable default implementation so adding the method is non-breaking; note the breaking change in the PR description.
validated_findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported plugins log.Logger interface breaks external implementers
validated_findings.trigger: Any code outside this repository tree (e.g. Grafana Enterprise or other consumers of pkg/plugins/log) that implements plog.Logger and passes it to NewLoggerMiddleware or backendplugin logging is compiled against the new interface.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Claim about breaking external implementers of plog.Logger interface. However, this is an internal package (`pkg/plugins/log`) and there's no evidence of external consumers. The patch provides implementations for all in-tree types (TestLogger, grafanaInfraLogWrapper). Breaking change concern is speculative without proof of external usage.
